chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, raised it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
He said: The wedding feast (Waleema) for one day is a mark of honor, and for two days it is prestige, and for three days it is showing-off and seeking fame.

key_terms.الْوَلِيمَةُ: The wedding feast or banquet hosted by the groom's family
key_terms.رِيَاءٌ: Showing off, performing deeds for the sake of public display
key_terms.سُمْعَةٌ: Seeking fame or reputation among people
key_terms.مَكْرُمَةٌ: An act of honor or generosity

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the duration of a wedding feast to avoid showing off?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a nuanced social ethic where the wedding feast (Waleema) transitions from a virtuous act of hospitality to a blameworthy display of vanity if prolonged beyond two days. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing social generosity with spiritual sincerity, warning against the corruption of intention (niyyah) in public rituals. The distinction highlights the danger of 'sum'ah' (seeking fame) in communal celebrations, a key theme in Shia moral jurisprudence.
